headline: KINROSS GOLD Q2: $2.24B REVENUE, $726M FREE CASH FLOW — +59% EARNINGS BEAT AT $4,483 GOLD, RECORD $2.7B CASH POSITION (NYSE/TSX: KGC)
snippet: Kinross Gold (NYSE/TSX: KGC) reported Q2 2026 earnings of $0.71 per share on July 31, beating the $0.66 consensus, with net earnings of $844.2 million (+59% year-over-year) on revenue of $2.24 billion — powered by a 37% increase in realized gold prices to $4,483 per ounce. Free cash flow reached $726 million in Q2 alone, lifting H1 2026 cumulative FCF to $1.5 billion and pushing cash to a record $2.7 billion with net cash of $1.9 billion. Production of 492,326 gold equivalent ounces at $1,352 per ounce cost of sales delivered over $3,100 per-ounce margins despite a 4% production decline year-over-year; full-year guidance was reaffirmed and the company returned $275 million to shareholders in the quarter. This is the result that validates the sector re-rating thesis: a producer running at sub-$1,400 costs against a $4,400+ gold price generates free cash flow at a scale that completely changes what self-funded growth looks like.

headline: ELDORADO Q2: SKOURIES COPPER-GOLD FIRST POUR ON TRACK FOR Q3 — Greece's Biggest New Mine Nears Commissioning With 2,948 On Site (TSX/NYSE: ELD)
snippet: Eldorado Gold (NYSE/TSX: ELD) confirmed on July 31 that Skouries — its $4 billion copper-gold mine in northern Greece and arguably the most significant new copper-gold development in Europe in decades — remains on schedule to produce its first copper-gold concentrate in Q3 2026, with commercial production targeted for Q4 2026. The project now has 2,948 personnel on site, including 515 Skouries-dedicated employees; process plant teams completed theoretical training and are in hands-on job familiarization mode. Q2 2026 production was 104,616 ounces of gold, with free cash flow negative $334.1 million as expected given Skouries' final development spend, though FCF excluding major projects was a positive $40.9 million. First-year Skouries production is guided at 60,000-100,000 oz gold and 20-40 million pounds copper — at current prices, a meaningful addition to group cash generation from day one, and a transformational moment for a company that has been building toward this for a decade.

headline: ENDEAVOUR MINING H1: $761M FREE CASH FLOW, $2.57B REVENUE — Record $301M Returned to Shareholders at $4,579 Realized Gold, AISC $1,871 (TSX/LSE: EDV)
snippet: Endeavour Mining (TSX/LSE: EDV) released H1 2026 results on July 30 that illustrate exactly what a high-margin West Africa gold producer looks like at $4,579 per ounce realized gold: $2,569 million in revenue (up $519 million from H1 2025), adjusted EBITDA of $1,611 million (+38%), adjusted net earnings of $672 million (+69%), operating cash flow of $1,055 million (+41%), and record free cash flow of $761 million (+48%). AISC of $1,871/oz against the $4,579 realized price delivers $2,708 per-ounce margins. Half-year shareholder returns reached a record $301 million, comprising a $0.95 per share dividend and $71 million in buybacks. Production of 564,000 ounces positions the company comfortably inside full-year guidance. For retail investors tracking West Africa producers, Endeavour demonstrates how high gold prices are compressing payback periods and unlocking shareholder returns that were theoretical twelve months ago.

headline: DPM METALS Q2 RECORD FCF — VAREŠ SILVER MINE ON TRACK FOR FULL PRODUCTION BY YEAR-END AS BREVENE SOUTH PORPHYRY ADDS EXPLORATION UPSIDE (TSX: DPM)
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM), the European-focused polymetallic producer, reported record Q2 2026 free cash flow and earnings on July 31 alongside confirmation that the Vareš Silver Project in Bosnia and Herzegovina remains on track to achieve full production by year-end 2026. The earnings follow DPM's June 2026 Brevene South Porphyry discovery at Chelopech, Bulgaria, where initial drilling returned 713 metres at 2.52 g/t AuEq (comprising 1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu) — the company's fourth significant discovery since 2023 in the Western Tethyan Belt. The combination of record operating results, a production growth catalyst at Vareš, and a major new porphyry discovery in the same reporting window makes DPM one of the more compelling small-to-mid-cap producer updates of this Q2 earnings season — particularly for investors looking for European exposure outside the Canadian senior gold producers.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER: 7th CONSECUTIVE RECORD EBITDA — Board Approves $45M Mantoverde Pyrite Project to Cut Acid Use 20%, Boost Output 3,500t/yr (TSX: CS)
snippet: Capstone Copper (TSX: CS) delivered a seventh consecutive quarter of record adjusted EBITDA in Q2 2026, with strong operational performance across Mantoverde and Mantos Blancos in Chile and Cozamin in Mexico at copper prices near $6.40 per pound. The board approved the Mantoverde Pyrite Augmentation (MVPA) project — a $45 million initiative targeted for completion in early 2028 that would reduce sulphuric acid consumption by approximately 20% and increase copper cathode production by ~3,500 tonnes per year, improving unit economics materially. The MV Optimized Project progressed on plan with the sulphide project tie-in expected in Q3 2026 at an unchanged $176 million total cost. Seven consecutive record EBITDA quarters at a pure-play TSX copper producer represents exactly the kind of operational credibility that attracts institutional re-rating, and the Grasberg-driven copper deficit shows no signs of resolving before 2027.

headline: COPPER AT $6.44/LB — GRASBERG FORCE MAJEURE CLAIMS 591,000 TONNES THROUGH YEAR-END, FREEPORT FULL CAPACITY NOT UNTIL 2027 (FCX, TECK, GLEN)
snippet: Copper held at $6.44 per pound on July 30, 2026 — up more than 14% year-to-date — as the extended consequences of Freeport-McMoRan's force majeure declaration at the Grasberg mine in September 2025 continue to drain global supply. Benchmark Minerals estimates approximately 591,000 tonnes of refined copper output has been lost through the force majeure period, tipping the global refined market into a structural deficit. Freeport cut its 2026 production guidance by 35% and now targets a return to full capacity only by the end of 2027, meaning near-term supply cannot meaningfully recover. LME inventories have fallen sharply as the structural imbalance shows up in stock drawdowns. Mining equity performance has followed: Teck Resources rose as much as 6.1%, Glencore gained 4.6%, Freeport-McMoRan climbed 4.1%, and Southern Copper added 3.7% in recent sessions as markets price in extended tightness. For junior copper developers with resources in permitting, this is the window where project values get re-rated.

headline: T2 METALS DRILLS AURORA FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 15 YEARS — Tombstone Gold Belt, Yukon: 8 Gold-Antimony-Copper Targets Under the Bit, Shawn Ryan-Mapped Ground (TSXV: TWO)
snippet: T2 Metals Corp. (TSXV: TWO) announced July 30 that drilling has commenced at its Aurora Gold-Silver Project in Yukon's Tombstone Gold Belt — the company's first drill program in the Yukon and the first drilling at Aurora in over 15 years. The project is centered on the Antimony Mountain Stock, a Tombstone Plutonic Suite intrusion associated with reduced intrusion-related gold systems (RIRGS) — the same geological framework that produced Fort Knox and Dublin Gulch. Shawn Ryan and other past explorers identified eight significant gold-bearing prospects across the project through soil and rock chip sampling; a 2026 summer mapping, prospecting, and sampling program identified new zones of gold, copper, and antimony mineralization. The maiden drill program is testing several of these prospects for the first time, making Aurora a true greenfield discovery opportunity in one of North America's most prolific and under-drilled gold belts.

headline: CAMECO REPORTS Q2 TODAY: URANIUM AT $86.60/LB (+21% YOY) — Kazatomprom Cut 10%, McArthur River Restored, AI Hyperscaler Nuclear PPAs Accelerate (NYSE/TSX: CCJ)
snippet: Cameco Corporation (NYSE/TSX: CCJ) reports Q2 2026 earnings on July 31 with uranium spot prices at $86.60 per pound — up 20.95% year-over-year — as the nuclear fuel market maintains structural tightness driven by supply discipline from both major producers. Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer, intentionally cut its 2026 production guidance by 10% to support price stability. Cameco's own McArthur River mine experienced a May 2026 logistics disruption from flooding, but the company established an alternate route and restored full production quickly. Q1 2026 uranium sales volumes rose 13% to 7.8 million pounds at a $65.45/lb realized price, with 2026 guidance calling for 29-32 million pounds at $85-89/lb — a significant step-change from $62.11/lb realized in 2025. Three catalysts define the July uranium setup: Cameco's Q2 results today, the Section 232 framework status, and ongoing hyperscaler nuclear power purchase agreement announcements from Meta and Microsoft.

headline: GOLD FELL 28% FROM $5,596 ATH — PBOC BUYS 14.93 TONNES FOR 20th STRAIGHT MONTH, WGC FAIR VALUE $4,100, GOLDMAN YEAR-END TARGET $4,900
snippet: Gold's correction from its January 2026 all-time high of $5,595.92 to near $4,066 — a 28% drawdown — has unnerved retail investors, but GoldSilver.com's July 2026 analysis argues the structural case remains fully intact. The primary driver was the US-Iran conflict raising energy prices, which pushed inflation higher, prompted a more hawkish Fed (rates held at 3.75%), and increased real yields — the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. Despite the correction, central bank demand is structurally undiminished: the People's Bank of China added 14.93 tonnes in June 2026, its 20th consecutive month of purchases and its largest single-month addition since 2023. The World Gold Council's Valuation Framework puts gold's fair value at approximately $4,100; Goldman Sachs targets $4,900 by year-end 2026 and J.P. Morgan's Q4 target is $4,500. For retail investors sitting on losses from Q1 highs, the data suggests the correction is consistent with prior bull market drawdowns — not a structural trend reversal.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT: 215M-OZ RECORD SHORTFALL, $59.10 ON JULY 30 — China Strategic Reclassification + Solar Demand Set Up the Next Leg
snippet: The global silver market is heading for its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026, projected at 215 million ounces — the largest structural shortfall on record — as demand from solar panels, electric vehicles, and electronics continues to outpace the structural limitations of silver mine supply. Silver traded at $59.10 per ounce on July 30, 2026, up 2.58% on the day, recovering from its January 2026 high near $121/oz. Two specific catalysts are identified for the next move higher: China's January 2026 reclassification of silver from an ordinary commodity to a strategic material — creating state purchasing programs outside commercial supply channels — and the supply constraint that approximately 70% of global silver production is a byproduct of copper, lead, and zinc mining and cannot be materially scaled even at $59+ spot prices. GoldSilver lead analyst Alan Hibbard forecasts silver above $100 in 2026 as deficits compound and strategic buyers accumulate.
